constraints: Use generated prime-order curves with trace not in {0,1} and j not in {0,1728}.
Use 31 independent random-scalar and 31 random-x null factor bases per curve.
Use exact four- and eight-term supports; unordered occupancy is a sizing control only.
Measure online work under four preregistered support-order permutations and retain all failed targets.
Treat results as TOY-EVIDENCE and prohibit split-compression, exponent, deployment, rank, or descent claims unless separately measured.
research_question.decision_target: Decide whether any frozen coordinate family has unusually high sign-complete eight-term coverage/frontier efficiency relative to paired null distributions after special-curve and support-order confounds are removed.
research_question.motivation: EXP-ECDLP-RECURSIVE-001 verified a sign-complete m=8 coverage/first-witness signal, but every passing four-term support was maximal, one curve was anomalous, and one-draw random controls varied too widely for family inference.

curve_families: generated non-supersingular, non-anomalous, non-special-j prime-order short-Weierstrass curves
field_types: prime fields constrained to p mod 4 = 3
methods: exact signed four- and eight-term support

research_question.title: Null-calibrated recursive coverage on non-special curves
